title: Effect of Video-Assisted Preoperative Patient Education on Patient Understanding, Satisfaction, and Anxiety Before Robot-Assisted Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
Before total knee replacement surgery, patients receive information from their surgeon about the planned procedure, possible risks, expected benefits, and the postoperative recovery process. However, previous studies have shown that many patients do not remember all of the information provided during the consultation and may still have questions or concerns before surgery.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether an additional educational video can improve the standard preoperative informed consent process for patients undergoing robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty. We will evaluate whether patients who watch the video have a better understanding of the planned procedure, are more satisfied with the informed consent process, and experience less anxiety before surgery.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will receive the standard preoperative informed consent provided by their surgeon, while the other group will receive the same standard informed consent plus an additional educational video about robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty.

After the informed consent process, all participants will complete questionnaires assessing their understanding of the procedure, their satisfaction with the information provided, and their level of preoperative anxiety.

Participation in the study will not affect the planned surgical procedure or the standard medical care received by the participants. All study data will be handled confidentially and stored in a pseudonymized form.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Scheduled for primary robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty due to primary knee osteoarthritis.
Ability to understand the patient information and to complete the study questionnaires independently.
Sufficient proficiency in the German language.
Provision of written informed consent for study participation.
Willingness to participate in all study-related assessments.
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 18 years.
Inability to provide informed consent.
Previous total knee arthroplasty of the contralateral knee.
Insufficient German language proficiency to understand the patient information and complete the study questionnaires independently.
Planned revision total knee arthroplasty or other complex revision procedures.
Severe cognitive impairment or neurological or psychiatric disorders that preclude reliable completion of the study questionnaires or the provision of informed consent.
Previous participation in this study.
